narrative_events.details: The opening invokes Gaṇeśa as complete yoga, giver of siddhis, heart-resident of yogins, the human/elephant form with attributed human and attribute-free elephant aspects; salutations include Śiva, Viṣṇu, Sūrya, Śakti, Brahmā, Śeṣa, Nara and Nārāyaṇa and the gods, yogins and sages.
narrative_events.outcome: Invocations establish the local teaching frame.

narrative_events.details: Fearful of Kali faults and instructed by Brahmā, Śaunaka and other sages reside at Naimiṣa with Vedic study, five sacrifices and daily/occasional duties. Sūta arrives, marvels at their conduct, bows, praises the sight of their feet as liberating, and accepts their offered seat and reciprocal welcome.
narrative_events.outcome: Sūta is seated as narrator.

narrative_events.details: Śaunaka calls Vyāsa an incarnation of Nārāyaṇa, divider of Veda and Purāṇas; Sūta learned Purāṇas and histories from him. Requested to recite, Sūta credits his teacher and tells many accounts and doctrines associated with the four human aims; the listeners rejoice.
narrative_events.outcome: Many narratives have been heard before the present question.

narrative_events.details: Hearing differing accounts that call Śiva, Viṣṇu, Sūrya, Śakti, Gaṇeśa, Virāj, Brahman, yoga, knowledge, action, self, breath, food, mind, intellect, Sāṃkhya or Svānanda supreme leaves the sages uncertain. Śaunaka asks for one scripturally accepted conclusion; Sūta introduces Mudgala’s teaching as that essence.
narrative_events.outcome: The Mudgala–Dakṣa frame is introduced.

narrative_events.details: Sūta briefly previews the ruined sacrifice: Rudra’s forces defeat gods, Vīrabhadra beheads Dakṣa, Brahmā conciliates Śiva and Śiva revives Dakṣa through yoga. Distressed and curse-confused Dakṣa receives the Gaṇeśa devotee Mudgala, addresses him as Āṅgirasa and asks help; Mudgala tells him to remember Vighnarāja.
narrative_events.outcome: The damaged Dakṣa seeks instruction; chapters2–4 retrospectively explain this outcome.

narrative_events.details: Dakṣa says the curse erased his knowledge and office; Mudgala’s presence brings some awareness and prompts his questions about Vighnapati. The sages request the cause. Sūta says Dakṣa is one of Brahmā’s ten sons and was made chief of Prajāpatis, then became proud.
narrative_events.outcome: Pride in office precedes the insult.

narrative_events.details: At Śiva’s Kailāsa assembly, Viṣṇu sits left, Brahmā right, Nandin-led Gaṇas nearby; Vasiṣṭha praises, Nārada-led singers sing, Apsarases dance. Śiva greets Dakṣa verbally but does not bow. Dakṣa invokes his father-in-law status, treats Śiva as son-like, denounces Śiva’s conduct and appearance, and ignores Brahmā’s rebuke.
narrative_events.outcome: Dakṣa’s hostile speech provokes Nandin.

narrative_events.details: Nandikeśvara condemns the slander, says Śiva plays with māyā without its faults, and curses Dakṣa to lose knowledge, obtain a goat face through the mouth that slandered Śiva, and lose his kingdom.
narrative_events.outcome: Nandin announces the curse conditions and outcomes.

narrative_events.details: Dakṣa replies that Śiva’s followers lack proper conduct and curses Śaivas to ignorance, Kali-age heterodoxy, matted hair, nakedness, ash, indulgence and hell. Brahmā rebukes him; Dakṣa leaves angry, the assembly disperses unhappy and Śiva is distressed. The precise study-related clause at42 is separately retained as unresolved.
narrative_events.outcome: Mutual curses and dispersal close the assembly episode.

narrative_events.details: Sūta frames non-devotion to Vighneśa as the cause of obstruction. At home Dakṣa wants to humble Śiva. Nārada recommends Bṛhaspatisava excluding Śiva’s sacrificial share; Dakṣa adopts it. Viṣṇu, gods, Gandharvas, Brahmins and Kaśyapa-led sons-in-law with wives gather. Both Gaṇeśa and Śiva are excluded, and all forget Gaṇeśa amid coming pride.
narrative_events.outcome: An exclusionary Bṛhaspatisava begins.

narrative_events.details: Dadhīci warns that a sacrifice without Śiva is like a lifeless body. Dakṣa rejects him, appealing to Viṣṇu’s presence. Dadhīci foretells ruin, curses attendees to Kali-age heterodoxy and loss of duty ending in hell, curses Viṣṇu to supporting heterodox followers, and predicts divine defeat and sage distress. Dadhīci leaves with Gautama, Gālava, Vāmadeva, Dvita, Trita, Mārkaṇḍeya and Agastya; Viṣṇu consoles remaining attendees, and Bhṛgu-led sages proceed.
narrative_events.outcome: Śaiva sages depart; the remaining sacrifice proceeds.

narrative_events.details: Nārada goes to Kailāsa, asks Satī why she has not joined the festival where her sisters and their husbands rejoice, and says honor/dishonor is irrelevant in a father’s or husband’s home. Satī asks Śiva to accompany her. He warns that her father hates him and has not invited him, offering instead a local sacrifice if she creates sages/gods. She asks leave; he remains silent. She decides permission is unnecessary and leaves; amazed Śiva sends a vimāna accepting what will occur.
narrative_events.outcome: Satī goes despite warning and absence of explicit permission.

narrative_events.details: Satī arrives by vimāna and is welcomed by mother, father, sisters and kin. Dakṣa welcomes her; she objects that she came uninvited. He blames his mistaken marriage arrangement made on his father’s advice and Śiva’s faults, while asking her to remain. Seeing no Rudra share and hearing slander, she declares the rite fruitless and renounces the body derived from Dakṣa.
narrative_events.outcome: Satī rejects her paternal body after repeated slander.

narrative_events.details: Satī meditates on Śiva in her heart, burns her body with yoga-fire and reaches the divine abode. The narrator then says the goddess by her own māyā becomes Himācala’s daughter, meditates and performs severe austerity, and again obtains Śiva as husband as Pārvatī.
narrative_events.outcome: Body abandonment is followed by a retrospective summary of rebirth and remarriage.

narrative_events.details: Śiva waits under the banyan with Nandin and yogins; omens disturb them. Nārada praises Satī’s body-burning; his silence to the death question makes Śiva understand. Śiva grieves, calls himself powerless without Śakti, recalls pride in inseparable Ardhanārīśvara lordship and realizes he had failed to remember Vighnarāja.
narrative_events.outcome: Grief becomes recognition of pride and neglected Gaṇeśa worship.

narrative_events.details: Śiva meditates on a four-armed, elephant-faced, great-bodied, large-bellied Gaṇeśa wearing crown, earrings, gem-garland, navel Śeṣa, anklets and chest Cintāmaṇi, with Siddhi/Buddhi. His hymn calls Gaṇeśa obstacle-creator for non-devotees and remover for devotees, cosmic creator of guṇa-linked Brahmā/Viṣṇu/Śiva, and Svānanda resident. He asks restoration of capacity to act, stating he cannot even walk without Śakti.
narrative_events.outcome: Śiva petitions for restored power to act.

narrative_events.details: Gaṇeśa appears, attributes the obstruction to Śiva’s pride, and approves renewed remembrance and praise. He promises Śakti’s rebirth as Himācala’s daughter and remarriage as Satī/Pārvatī, Śiva’s empowered lordship through devotion/grace, and immediate appearance whenever Śiva remembers him; then disappears.
narrative_events.outcome: Śiva receives future reunion and present restoration of agency.

narrative_events.details: Restored to action and remembering Gaṇeśa, Śiva strikes his matted hair. Vīrabhadra arises with three heads, three feet and trident, bows as servant, receives the command to destroy Dakṣa and the sacrifice, laughs so the three worlds tremble, and creates innumerable Rudras from his body. Nandin-led Śiva Gaṇas follow.
narrative_events.outcome: Vīrabhadra and his generated Rudras march to the sacrifice.

narrative_events.details: Omens terrify sacrifice attendees. Vīrabhadra, Rudras, Nandin, Bhṛṅgiriṭi, Bhṛṅgin and Puṣpadanta attack; attendants flee, the pavilion is broken, gods/sages are beaten, wives are seized/beaten and taunted over husbands’ Śiva hostility, offerings eaten and altar defiled.
narrative_events.outcome: The sacrificial order is violently disrupted.

narrative_events.details: Śiva enters with bow/arrows and fights: he breaks Pūṣan’s teeth and removes Bhaga’s eyes. Nandin seizes Dharma, Bhṛṅgin Kaśyapa, Puṣpadanta beats Varuṇa, Bhairava seizes/fells Indra, Vīrabhadra fells Dakṣa. Viṣṇu fights and hurts Rudra/ghost forces; Śiva remembers Gaṇeśa and wounds Viṣṇu’s heart with arrows, felling him.
narrative_events.outcome: Viṣṇu is felled but then regains awareness.

narrative_events.details: Recovering, Viṣṇu releases the destructive Nārāyaṇa missile; Śiva releases Pāśupata. They fight in the sky and generate fire threatening earth and three worlds. Meanwhile Vīrabhadra treats Dakṣa as a sacrificial beast, cuts his head and offers it into fire. Viṣṇu hurls the cakra, which bows to Śiva and stops rather than striking him.
narrative_events.outcome: Dakṣa is beheaded; the cakra fails to attack Śiva.

narrative_events.details: Śiva raises his trident to kill Viṣṇu, but an unidentified heavenly voice forbids it and commands protection; Brahmā arrives, praises Śiva, warns against untimely destruction, and reconciles him with ashamed bowing Viṣṇu. Brahmā offers remaining oblations as Rudra’s share and asks restoration/restart. Śiva restores Bhaga’s eyes, makes Pūṣan a eater of ground food, and restores gods/sages/wives/servants to forms and radiance.
narrative_events.outcome: Viṣṇu survives and attendees are restored.

narrative_events.details: Because Dakṣa’s head was burnt, Śiva orders Bhṛṅgin to kill the first being he sees and bring its head. Bhṛṅgin sees a goat, kills it, brings its head; Śiva attaches it and revives Dakṣa. Brahmā prompts the now-humble Dakṣa to praise Śiva.
narrative_events.outcome: Dakṣa rises alive with a goat head.

narrative_events.details: Dakṣa’s hymn identifies Śiva with time-governed cosmic processes and asks pardon for pride. His goat-like speech delights Śiva, who restores his former human head, promises restored recognized Prajāpati chiefship, desired gifts and Śiva’s world to hymn-praisers, and fulfillment to one making the goat-like sound before him once. Śiva disappears, others return home, but Dakṣa remains distressed; the narrator explains temple bleating practice.
narrative_events.outcome: Human head and office restored; Dakṣa’s remaining distress leads to Mudgala teaching.

narrative_events.details: Mudgala calls Gaṇeśa universal mother/father and first-worshipped Jyeṣṭharāja/Vināyaka, resident in Svānanda; all others are his partial expressions. Pride in self-supremacy brings obstruction and lost office; contemplative recognition brings refuge and relief. Cintāmaṇi is explained as illuminator of mind’s five operations. Mudgala urges Dakṣa’s refuge; Dakṣa asks how to know/worship him.
narrative_events.outcome: A nested Śiva–Pārvatī teaching is requested.

narrative_events.details: At Kailāsa Pārvatī asks why universally honored Śiva meditates, knowing none above him. Śiva says he meditates day/night on heart-resident Svānanda Gaṇeśa beyond form/formlessness and mental/speech opposition. Pārvatī asks how such meditation works, adopts a disciple’s position and seeks realization; Śiva accepts her fitness for this path.
narrative_events.outcome: Pārvatī explicitly becomes a requesting disciple.

narrative_events.details: Dakṣa asks Mudgala to continue. Remembering Gaṇeśa, Śiva distinguishes mind-apprehended māyā from what transcends it, explains self-aware Svānanda and Cintāmaṇi’s illumination of five mental grounds, and says Gaṇeśa can be contemplated through non-separation yoga. Pārvatī says the compressed teaching is not understood and requests an easier detailed account of māyā-bound and transcendent Brahman; Śiva begins.
narrative_events.outcome: The question leads directly into creation teaching.

narrative_events.details: Śiva begins after praising Pārvatī’s Gaṇeśa interest. The teaching traces Brahman, self/other emergence and reflection, māyā as Buddhi and deluding Siddhi, illuminated by Gaṇeśa. Desire to become many yields body/embodied forms described as bindu and so’ham; these two cannot perform their functions without efficacy.
narrative_events.outcome: The future Prakṛti/Puruṣa pair lacks power to act.

narrative_events.details: The two perform severe austerity to their own true form for1,000 divine years. Gaṇeśa appears with trunk, large belly/ears, four arms and three eyes. Recognition lets them bow and hymn: formless trunk and formed body below neck, four arms explained through avyakta/sama/sat/asat principles, belly containing all, and feet through māyā/māyika. They ask him to remain in their heart, specify what duty to perform, and give intense devotion.
narrative_events.outcome: Prakṛti/Puruṣa ask direction and devotion.

narrative_events.details: Gaṇeśa grants their wishes and declares hymn rewards: four aims, nourishment, release from jail at100,000 recitations, destruction of harmful rites, desired fruit at21recitations for21days, and Brahmanhood for desireless reading. He names Prakṛti as source of creation, grants unbound devotion and gifts to her desireful/desireless devotees. Puruṣa receives so’ham identity, unbound devotion, grant-giving and yogic Brahmanhood-bestowal; he must implant efficacy-seed in Prakṛti for world creation. Creation, maintenance and destruction proceed at due times; they are called universal mother/father. Gaṇeśa disappears and they obey.
narrative_events.outcome: Cosmic duties and devotional grants enable subsequent creation.

narrative_events.details: Pārvatī asks what follows the divine disappearance. Śiva says Prakṛti and Puruṣa gain capacity and mutual affinity; she enchants him, he plants seed, she becomes pregnant and later gives birth to luminous Mahān/Mahat, eldest among tattvas and their inner principle.
narrative_events.outcome: Mahat is born in the explicitly cosmological genealogy.

narrative_events.details: Mahat creates Ahaṃkāra, divided into sattva/rajas/tamas and knowledge/action/material powers. The tamasic sequence produces sound/space, touch/wind, form/fire, taste/water, smell/earth and a five-element body. The text’s conceptual generation is preserved as Śiva’s cosmogony.
narrative_events.outcome: Ahaṃkāra’s three powers generate subtle/elemental structure.

narrative_events.details: Rājasic power creates sensory organs tongue/eye/skin/nose/ear, action organs hands/feet/anus/speech/generative organ and five breaths prāṇa/vyāna/apāna/udāna/samāna. Sāttvic power creates sensory deities directions/Vāyu/Varuṇa/Aśvins/Sūrya and action deities Agni/Viṣṇu/Prajāpāla/Indra/Mitra; lists are retained without inventing one-to-one mappings.
narrative_events.outcome: Ten listed presiding deities and functional organs appear.

narrative_events.details: The primordial tattva deities lack knowledge and cannot create. Prakṛti and Puruṣa give the one-syllable Gaṇeśa mantra with ritual procedure. Severe austerity of unspecified duration wins appearance. Their hymn addresses Vakratunda through opposed theological pairs and describes noose/goad/tusk/abhaya, four arms, large ears/belly, one tusk and elephant face. They stand ready for his answer.
narrative_events.outcome: Teachers and mantra lead to manifestation and hymn.

narrative_events.details: Gaṇeśa offers their desired boon and promises hymn hearers/readers siddhis, knowledge, wealth, wife, good sons, liberation and victory as requested. Ādiṛṣis/tattvas ask unwavering devotion, creative capacity, ability to give devotees siddhis, fulfillment and perpetual freedom from bondage. Gaṇeśa explicitly grants all requests and disappears.
narrative_events.outcome: The tattvas receive the requested compound boon.

narrative_events.details: After sorrow at disappearance, boon-enlightened tattvas mutually interpenetrate and form an egg. Guṇeśa arises within, emits waters, grows full-bodied and splits the egg by radiance; his universal limbs, cosmic pores, fourth/mahākāraṇa state and lordship of guṇas are described. Activity produces names Nārāyaṇa/Brahma/Mahādeva/Sūrya/Ādiśakti in this cosmic explanation, not automatic identity with each separately established actor. Ignorance prompts severe Gaṇeśa meditation and one-syllable japa over an unspecified long time; Gaṇeśa appears and offers a boon.
narrative_events.outcome: Guṇeśa emerges and becomes a boon petitioner.

narrative_events.details: Guṇeśa hymns Gaṇeśa as tranquil yoga lord through form/without-form and various cosmic/doctrinal descriptions, distinguishing those as partial manifestations. He calls sight/tapas fruitful and requests firm devotion destroying delusion, creative capacity, fulfilling devotees’ wishes and unobstructed works.
narrative_events.outcome: Requested devotion and creative power are explicit.

narrative_events.details: Gaṇeśa grants devotion, varied creation without obstruction, gift-giving, and his appearance when a great task arises. Guṇeśa’s hymn is named Stutisāraka, promising Brahmanhood/siddhis, desires to desireful users and liberation to desireless devotees; three-times-daily reading makes Gaṇeśa attainable. He disappears; Guṇeśa feels separation.
narrative_events.outcome: The creative boon is granted; Guṇeśa’s next actions begin9.

narrative_events.details: Boon-enlightened Guṇeśa turns to creation. Vedas emerge from his breath; he creates the equal-element causal sleep-state world called Pradhāna, tamasic and ignorant of duty. It performs1,000divine-year tapas, receives Gaṇeśa’s appearance, worships/praises and gets yogic capacity. Vedas independently perform severe tapas and worship: Ṛg uses Brahmaṇaspati-sūkta, Yajus Gaṇeśa-śānti, Sāman eight-name praise, Atharvan Atharvaśīrṣa. Gaṇeśa grants universal teacher-standing, accepted/praised worldwide.
narrative_events.outcome: Pradhāna and Vedas receive differentiated powers.

narrative_events.details: Asked what Pradhāna does, Śiva says it creates subtle sāttvic Hiraṇyagarbha/dream world, enclosed by subtle principles. Lacking knowledge, Hiraṇyagarbha performs difficult tapas and receives the desired, unspecified boon/capacity. It creates gross rājasic waking world; this also lacks knowledge, performs tapas, receives appearance, worships and gains a boon/capacity. Gross world becomes many three-state worlds; innumerable eggs emerge from Guṇeśa’s pores. The enclosing/enclosed unity is called Prakṛti/Brahma-bindu.
narrative_events.outcome: Causal→subtle→gross creation proceeds through distinct tapas/boons.

narrative_events.details: Gross waking creates space, then wind, fire, water and earth with sound/touch/form/taste/smell. Mutual entering gives earth5qualities, water4,fire3,wind2,space1. Prakṛti has eight envelope forms empowered by reflected Guṇeśa; Virāṭ arises in the egg. Earth’s displayed extent is50crore and successive envelopes are tenfold:water/fire/wind/space/waking-ego/dream-Mahat/sleep-māyā. Final order encloses Virāṭ by earth, earth by water, water by fire, fire by wind, wind by space, space by ego, ego by Mahat, Mahat by māyā. Countless such eggs surround Guṇeśa.
narrative_events.outcome: The eight-envelope egg and its cosmic inhabitant are established.

narrative_events.details: Pārvatī asks Virāṭ’s form. Śiva describes5croreyojana body and14worlds:feet Pātāla,ankles Rasātala,heels Mahātala,shanks Talātala,knees Sutala,thighs Vitala,waist-junction Atala,waist Bhūloka,navel Bhuvar,heart Svar,neck Mahar,mouth Jana,forehead Tapo,head Satya. Thousands of heads/faces/feet/hands/ears/bellies and universal pervasion are described, with external waking Vaiśvānara, inner dream Hiraṇyagarbha, sleep-state Īśvara and fourth self-state.
narrative_events.outcome: Virāṭ body-world and state correspondences are established.

narrative_events.details: Ignorant Virāṭ meditates in his heart with the one-syllable procedure and performs1,000divine-year severe tapas. Gaṇeśa appears and offers a boon. Virāṭ bows, credits sight with fulfilled birth/tapas/knowledge/body, and hymns the deity through Siddhi/Buddhi lordship, cosmic deity forms, māyā/transcendent qualities and source-of-knowledge powers.
narrative_events.outcome: Virāṭ petitions through worship and praise.

narrative_events.details: Gaṇeśa declares hymn rewards of siddhi, desired gifts and enjoyment/liberation for faithful reading/hearing. Virāṭ asks firm devotion destroying delusion, capacity for creation/preservation/destruction, unequaled lordship and fulfillment. Gaṇeśa says so be it and disappears; Virāṭ happily contemplates him. Śiva says other cosmic eggs’ Virāṭs likewise perform tapas and receive unobstructed duties, while cosmic eggs are innumerable.
narrative_events.outcome: Virāṭ’s compound cosmic boon is granted.

narrative_events.details: Pārvatī asks Virāṭ’s creation and meditation method; Dakṣa asks Mudgala to continue. Śiva says Virāṭ remembers Gaṇeśa and creates Brahmā from navel,Viṣṇu from mouth,Hara from eye,Śakti/Pārvatī from left side,Sūrya from right. Ignorant of self and origin, five wander long in darkness, then contemplate whatever is the root and undertake severe tapas. Gaṇeśa enters inwardly, giving heart-vision of a one-syllable seed-mantra; japa brings pure knowledge.
narrative_events.outcome: Five receive the inwardly revealed mantra rather than an invented external guru.

narrative_events.details: After1,000divine years Gaṇeśa manifests with immeasurable solar radiance,trunk,four arms,large belly,adornments/weapons,Siddhi/Buddhi and mouse vehicle. The five fear burning and call on Vighneśa; he makes his form gentle, giving perception and recognition. They hymn names including Heramba/Dhundhirāja/Vināyaka and opposed cosmic/yogic states, seek protection and fall silent.
narrative_events.outcome: Fright is relieved by a gentle form and knowledge.

narrative_events.details: Gaṇeśa offers their desired boon and hymn fruits:four aims,sons/grandsons,prosperity,final Svānanda; prison release at7dailyrecitations for21days; divine honor from1/2/3times-dailyreading; no fear of harmful rites at21recitations for21days; wealth/grain,health,cattle and desired ends. The five ask firm devotion preventing māyā-affliction,direction,varied power,devotee wish fulfillment and a place of perpetual bliss.
narrative_events.outcome: The common request precedes individual cosmic assignments.

narrative_events.details: Gaṇeśa grants individual roles:four-faced rājasic Brahmā creates,lives Satyaloka and rides haṃsa with Vedic knowledge;four-armed sāttvic Viṣṇu preserves,lives Vaikuṇṭha,rides Garuḍa and has many incarnations;five-faced tāmasic Hara destroys,lives Kailāsa,rides bull and burns all by third eye;thousand-rayed Sūrya activates karma/six seasons,is planet-king,rain-root,resides Sauraloka and rides a horse-adorned chariot;four-armed Śakti/Mahāmāyā deludes through enjoyment/liberation,resides Śaktiloka and rides lion. Gaṇeśa promises appearance at great tasks,grants weapons/ornaments,varied capacities and fulfilled resolve,and disappears. Five rejoice as empowered wish-fulfillers.
narrative_events.outcome: Five cosmic functions,stations,mounts and powers are assigned.
